subject: Release shelf criteria + network quiet policy for AtlasRetail Private upgrade
messages:
From: Tyler O'Brien <tyler.obrien@atlasretail.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: AtlasRetail maintenance request - VPC private upgrade

Hi Monica / Karthik,

We are preparing the private-agent bundle upgrade for our AtlasRetail VPC that includes the runtime 2.4.1 -> 2.5.0 bump and the security kernel backports. Before we lock a window with NetOps, we need documented criteria that Redwood will use to either: 1) shelf the release (postpone), or 2) proceed with a rollback if telemetry gating fails. AtlasRetail needs this for our internal change approvals.

Key constraints from our side:
- Preferred narrow maintenance windows: Weeknights 01:00-04:00 UTC or Saturdays 02:00-06:00 UTC
- Minimal traffic diversion (can't keep more than 20% of traffic routed elsewhere for >6 hours)
- Audit evidence for any rollback decision (what was run, who approved)

I've attached the maintenance request form (atlas_maintenance_request.pdf) with our proposed window. Can you send back a short checklist and the holdpoint criteria (telemetry gates + netops quiet policy) so we can share with change board?

Thanks,
Tyler
Ops Lead, AtlasRetail

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: AtlasRetail maintenance request - VPC private upgrade

Thanks Tyler — appreciate the clear constraints. I pulled together a short draft of the decision criteria and the network "quiet window" expectations. 

I'll summarise high level here and attach a working doc (shelf_criteria_draft.md) for operational sign-off:

1) Safety holdpoints (minimum):
   - Canary (1% traffic): pass acceptance checks for 90 minutes + no error spike >1.5x baseline
   - Post-canary hold (24 hours): key telemetry (tail latency, p50/p95, error-rate) stable within agreed deltas
   - Full rollout gating: automated health checks + manual NetOps sign-off if cross-region network changes were applied
   - Rollback window: we require an explicit rollback decision within 6 hours of a failed gating check unless agreed otherwise

2) Release-shelf criteria (what causes us to postpone before starting):
   - Missing preflight results (integration smoke or failing dependency matrix)
   - Known incompatible pin with customer-stated pinned model version or quantization profile
   - NetOps reports outstanding routing conflicts or capacity shortfalls

3) Network quiet policy (NetOps expectations):
   - Route changes/draining must be scheduled inside the agreed maintenance window and completed within the first 2 hours of the window
   - No large-scale BGP/ACL changes during the 24h post-canary unless emergency
   - Captured netplan snapshot to be attached (netplan_snapshot.png) and kept as evidence

I've attached the draft doc and the netplan snapshot for context. Karthik / Marissa / Irene — can you review and add final technical gating rules and the official NetOps quiet policy?

Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

On Fri, May 14, 2026 at 11:03 AM Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com> wrote:
> I've attached the draft doc and the netplan snapshot for context. Karthik / Marissa / Irene — can you review and add final technical gating rules and the official NetOps quiet policy?

Quick technical notes / suggested additions to the gating checklist:

- Pin compatibility check: verify customer pinned model hashes (if customer has a pinned model) against runtime ABI for 2.5.0. If hash mismatch then shelf; do NOT auto-translate pins.
- KV cache migration: run a small-scale cache warmup during canary to validate de/serialization. Failure mode: partial KV miss spike > 10% over baseline -> rollback.
- Leader-election drift check: small windows of leader churn acceptable within first 30m; sustained leader flaps > 3 events in 30m -> fail canary.
- Telemetry gating implementation: use the existing rollout-gate pipeline (ops-rollout-check) and require two consecutive green runs spaced by 10 minutes.
- Fast rollback path: snapshot agent config + pinset before starting and publish a single-line rollback command in the playbook (we'll keep this secret to limit accidental runs).

Operational timeline suggestion for the windows you gave Tyler:
- Weeknight window (01:00-04:00 UTC): canary in first hour, hold until 02:00 for quick rollback if needed, then continue staged rollout 02:00-04:00 with 30m increments.
- Saturday longer window: use first 2 hours for thorough canary + extended telemetry (4h) then proceed.

I'll add a short playbook snippet to the draft and push the final before EOD.

—Karthik
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference

Adding the compliance and evidence side:

- Audit trail: every gating decision must be recorded with timestamped sign-off (Slack thread ok for immediate but Confluence decision note required within 24h).
- SOC2 / customer evidence: capture rollout logs, netplan snapshot, canary telemetry dumps and the exact rollback command used (if executed). We should attach these artifacts to the DocuSign change package for AtlasRetail.
- Telemetry thresholds: define three severity bands (green/yellow/red) and require that any red triggers an immediate rollback. Yellow requires Ops lead manual approval to continue.
- Post-rollback confirmation: if rollback is executed, run a short verification suite and capture a signed-off incident note before re-scheduling.

Monica — from a compliance perspective we also want the customer's security contact on the approval loop; Tyler, please confirm who that is so we can include them on the DocuSign envelope.

Irene Choi
Principal PM, Security & Compliance
